questions.stem: What does CI stand for in CI/CD?
What does CD stand for in CI/CD?
questions.explanation: CD stands for Continuous Delivery or Continuous Deployment.

questions.stem: What was the challenge with the traditional development and implementation life cycle once coding was complete?
options: The remaining steps were time-consuming, with many manual processes and dependencies on departments for review, approval and deployment
Developers had no access to version control
Code could not be packaged for production
Testing was not permitted before deployment
Deployments could only happen once a year
questions.explanation: After development, packaging, testing and deployment relied on slow manual processes and cross-department dependencies, with a constant risk of human error.

questions.stem: In the example where five deployments are carried out at the same time, four go smoothly and the fifth breaks the other four. What does this illustrate?
options: That deployments should always be done in batches of five
That testing is unnecessary for small changes
That automated pipelines cause more failures than manual ones
That version control cannot handle parallel work
That with manual processes one deployment can affect other people's code as well
questions.explanation: The incident shows how manual, human-driven deployments can impact other deployments, which is the risk CI/CD is designed to remove.

questions.stem: Once development is done and code is pushed into the CI process, what does CI do?
options: Deploys the code straight to production
Builds and tests the code before passing it to the CD process
Requests manual approval from each department
questions.explanation: The CI process builds and tests the code, then hands it to the CD process.

questions.stem: What does the CD process do after receiving code from CI?
options: Builds, configures, packages and deploys it so that it meets all production-ready standards
Rolls the code back to the previous version
Sends the code to business users for sign-off
questions.explanation: CD builds, configures, packages and deploys the code in a way that fulfils production-ready standards.

questions.stem: With the help of CI/CD, how much has the release cycle for small deployments been reduced?
options: From weeks to a few days
From days or sometimes weeks to minutes
questions.explanation: A cycle that used to take days or even weeks can now be completed in minutes for small deployments.

questions.stem: Which development approach does CI/CD directly support, enabling mini code deployments?
questions.explanation: CI/CD directly supports agile development, so small, frequent code deployments can take place.

questions.stem: What is identified as the fundamental reason errors were inevitable in the traditional release process?
options: Human involvement in the manual steps
questions.explanation: Whenever there is human involvement, errors are inevitable, which is why automation through CI/CD is the answer.

questions.stem: What is said about the future of release management?
options: Manual review boards will return for safety
The future is CI/CD for any and every kind of release management
Release management will be replaced by data governance
Only large enterprises will need release management
Releases will be limited to once per quarter
questions.explanation: The closing statement is that the future is CI/CD for any or every kind of release management.
